clue.text: Affected by kick in a US military training base

parts.note: to boot something is to kick it
camp means affected or theatrically exaggerated

explanation.surface: Someone at an American army base is moved by a kick.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue gives the pieces in reverse order: 'by' only places the two side by side, and the kick goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough introductory training camp for American military recruits, now a general term for any intensive course.

clue.text: Beginning to fix home after end of tornado

indicators.note: the fix-and-home pieces follow the tornado's last letter
the end of the word tornado means its final letter only

parts.note: to rig is to fix dishonestly, as in rigging a vote
in means at home

explanation.surface: A homeowner starts repairs after a tornado has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: A source or starting point is a beginning; noun synonym.

clue.text: Short time ahead of it, a new moon

indicators.note: the time letter comes before the word it in the answer

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A new moon is due shortly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a new moon' reads as a lunar phase, but 'a' and 'new' are wordplay and 'moon' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn, so it is an example of a moon.

clue.text: Praise cooking devouring favourite hors d'oeuvre, perhaps

indicators.note: devouring means the shuffled letters swallow the favourite piece
cooking suggests the letters of praise being worked over into a new mix

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone praises the cook while eating a favourite starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' looks like part of the kitchen scene but scrambles PRAISE into APISER, which 'devouring' then wraps round the favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter dish eaten to sharpen the appetite; an hors d'oeuvre is one example, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Finishes drink below deck

indicators.note: in a down answer the drink piece sits below the deck piece

parts.note: a deck of cards is a pack
to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A sailor finishes a drink below deck on a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: To call it a day or stop working is to finish; phrasal verb synonym, third person to match.

clue.text: Month of gold rush

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a gust is a sudden rush of wind

explanation.surface: A gold rush lasting a month.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth month of the calendar year.

clue.text: A second photograph shows jelly

parts.note: pic is short for picture or photograph

explanation.surface: A second snapshot reveals a jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: A savoury jelly made from meat stock, used to set or glaze cold dishes.

clue.text: Turn round the bend and become very angry

definitions.meaning: to turn round the bend is to go crazy, losing one's mind
to fly into a frenzied rage

explanation.surface: A driver takes a corner and then loses their temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn round the bend' reads as steering a car, but 'round the bend' is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The slang idiom means both to go mad and to get wildly excited or furious.

clue.text: Visitor stumped nature reserve official

parts.note: ST is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for stumped
a ranger looks after a park or nature reserve

explanation.surface: A visitor puzzles the warden of a nature reserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumped' reads as baffled, but here it is the cricket dismissal, a batter put out by the wicketkeeper.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfamiliar newcomer or visitor; synonym.

clue.text: Burly jumper, say, in circus tent

parts.note: a burly person is big
a jumper, or sweater, is an example of a top

explanation.surface: A burly acrobat in a jumper performs under canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater, not someone who leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The large main marquee of a travelling circus.

clue.text: Famous film director appearing outside by a strange large rodent

indicators.note: appearing outside means the director's name wraps around the other letters

parts.note: Frank Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life

indicators.note: strange signals that the letters of by a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrated director turns up beside an odd giant rodent.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank Capra, Hollywood director of It's a Wonderful Life, splits in two; 'strange' rearranges BY A into YBA, which sits in the gap that 'appearing outside' opens.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American capybara is the largest living rodent.

clue.text: Ear complaint can fool American

parts.note: a tin is a can
a nit is a fool, short for nitwit

explanation.surface: A medical complaint about ears can make an American look foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' reads as a verb but it is the noun, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringing or buzzing in the ears is a medical condition, here called an ear complaint.

clue.text: Stick enthralling smart dog

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the stick piece holds the smart piece inside

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means fashionable or smart, as in the in crowd

explanation.surface: A walking stick fascinates a clever dog.
explanation.definitionFit: Canine is a noun for any member of the dog family.

clue.text: Crestfallen as Democrat is elected

parts.note: chosen for office, appointed

explanation.surface: A political party member is downcast that a Democrat won the vote.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling let down and dejected; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Pancake — declines cold one

parts.note: to drop is to decline or fall
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone refuses a cold pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'declines' reads as refuses, but it is falls. A drop scone is a small thick British griddle pancake.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for a Scotch pancake, made by dropping batter onto a griddle.

clue.text: Mainly old part of church viewed before storm

indicators.note: before puts the church piece ahead of the storm piece

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
to rage is to storm

explanation.surface: An ancient part of a church seen before a storm hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Generally, as a rule; adverb synonym meaning for the most part.

clue.text: Raise one northern fold

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a crease is a fold

explanation.surface: A northerner asks for a pay rise for a farm fold.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise is to make greater or higher; verb synonym.

clue.text: Rude Romany is on the move? There's no chance of that!

indicators.note: on the move signals the letters of the phrase travelling into a new order

explanation.surface: A traveller is on the road again, and someone scoffs at hopes of settling.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal retort saying something wished for will never happen.

clue.text: Ask about mission

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a quest is a mission

explanation.surface: An inquiry about a mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To request is to ask for something; verb synonym.

clue.text: Weird scene must involve a hand-holding event?

indicators.note: must involve means the shuffled letters take the a inside them
weird signals the letters of scene are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd scene at a gathering where people hold hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must involve' puts A inside SENCE, the anagram of SCENE from 'Weird'.
explanation.definitionFit: At a spiritualist meeting sitters often join hands around a table, so a playful description.

clue.text: Conservative rebels in periods of political instability?

parts.note: rises up, as rebels do

explanation.surface: Conservative rebels cause political turmoil.
explanation.definitionFit: Emergencies or times of severe trouble; political instability is one kind.

clue.text: Small trading centre, well-kept

parts.note: a mart is a market or trading centre

explanation.surface: A small market that is tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and well maintained in appearance; adjective synonym.

clue.text: Dominant woman, busy person chasing cat

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the busy person follows the cat

parts.note: a queen is a female cat
a busy bee is a busy person

explanation.surface: A bossy woman hurries after a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a woman who dominates her circle, like the ruler of a hive.

clue.text: Approaching tense hours of darkness

parts.note: nigh means near or approaching
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Tense hours as darkness draws near.
explanation.definitionFit: The period between dusk and dawn when it is dark.

clue.text: Boats at sea to get on, and wreck

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of boats are mixed

parts.note: to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Ships at sea grow old and are wrecked.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately damage or obstruct something; verb synonym.

clue.text: Broker handling king's silver

indicators.note: handling means holding in the hands, so the broker piece holds the king piece

parts.note: an agent acts as a broker
R stands for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A dealer handles the royal silver.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry, the term for silver or white.

clue.text: Pick and choose after start of sale

indicators.note: after puts the choose piece behind the sale's first letter
the start of sale means its first letter

parts.note: to elect is to choose

explanation.surface: A shopper picks and chooses once the sale begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pick and choose' reads as one idiom, but 'Pick' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick is to select; verb synonym.

clue.text: Agreements causing worry between judges

indicators.note: between places the worry piece inside the judges piece

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
to eat at someone is to worry them, as in what's eating you?

explanation.surface: Peace deals cause anxiety among judges.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal agreements between states are treaties.
